name: Stillwater Garden
location: Veluwe woodland edge, Netherlands · fictional garden
description: A private world of water, wild planting and quiet architecture. A complete fictional landscape concept.

budget.label: Landscape construction
budget.note: €18,000 earthworks + €12,000 drainage + €34,000 hardscape. All three subcontract packages included.

budget.label: Ground preparation & earthworks
budget.note: Included in Terra Forma. Protection, site preparation, grading and ordinary spoil allowance. Unforeseen contamination excluded.

budget.label: Drainage & irrigation distribution
budget.note: Included in Terra Forma. Drainage routes and irrigation pipework; below-ground rainwater storage is optional and additional.

budget.label: Paths, terraces & sunken lounge
budget.note: Included in Terra Forma. €19,500 stone supply + €14,500 bedding, laying, gravel and lounge construction.

budget.label: Limestone supply & fabrication
budget.note: Second-tier subquote: included in Stone & Line, itself included in Terra Forma. Never add this again.

budget.label: Charred-timber dining pavilion
budget.note: €23,000 timber, roof and fitting + €9,000 structural metalwork. Outdoor kitchen is additional and optional.

budget.label: Pavilion metalwork package
budget.note: Included in Timber Field. Fabrication and fitting allowance; final engineering remains a review gate.

budget.label: Optional outdoor kitchen
budget.note: Additional to the €32,000 pavilion. Images show this option; unselected in the base budget.

budget.label: Trees, meadow & woodland planting
budget.note: Trees €11,000 + perennials/grasses €12,500 + woodland understorey €6,000. Concept quantities, pending survey and nursery approval.

budget.label: Reflecting pool & water equipment
budget.note: Decorative water feature allowance, not a swimming pool. Includes lining, edge coordination and recirculation equipment.

budget.label: Garden lighting & controls
budget.note: Fixtures €7,200 + cabling/installation €3,000 + controls/commissioning €2,200. Final electrical design by appointed specialist.

budget.label: Outdoor furniture & objects
budget.note: Base €14,500; premium teak, upholstery and larger dining selection €22,500. Covers loose furniture only.

budget.label: Productive garden & oak beds
budget.note: Four raised beds, gravel working surface, trellis and starter planting. Hand-filled surface water butt included.

budget.label: Landscape design & coordination
budget.note: Concept, design development, specifications and six site reviews. Surveys, permits and specialist engineering excluded.

budget.label: First-year establishment care
budget.note: Eight scheduled visits, planting establishment review and seasonal handover. Not a low-maintenance guarantee.

budget.label: Client-held contingency
budget.note: Planning reserve held by the client; not a supplier commitment.

budget.label: Optional rainwater storage system
budget.note: Additional to the drainage package: underground tank, pump and connection allowance. Site feasibility review required.

budget.label: Unforeseen ground conditions
budget.note: Unpriced and excluded: contaminated spoil, unexpected obstructions and exceptional ground remediation.

slides.title:
Stillwater
Garden.
slides.subtitle: LANDSCAPES FOR A SLOWER LIFE
slides.body: A private world of water, wild planting and beautifully quiet architecture. Concept collection / September 2026

slides.title:
Step outside.
Feel elsewhere.
slides.subtitle: 01 / THE INVITATION
slides.body: For fictional clients Mira and Sebastiaan de Wilde, the garden becomes the most generous room of the house: a place for long lunches, unhurried walks and the simple pleasure of watching the seasons change.
points: Imagined location: wooded edge of the Dutch Veluwe
Illustrative garden plot: 1,400 m²
Demo 02 / Private residential landscape

slides.title:
A little untamed.
Entirely considered.
slides.subtitle: THE DESIGN BRIEF
slides.body: A garden with enough structure to feel composed and enough life to surprise you.
points: A place to gather: dining, cooking and conversation
A place to retreat: water, woodland and a quiet bench
A place to notice: flowers, shadows and seasonal change
A clear investment with traceable supplier packages

slides.title:
One garden.
Many small worlds.
slides.subtitle: THE LANDSCAPE AS A WHOLE
slides.body: Water is the still centre. A loose ribbon of meadow links a social terrace to a woodland edge, while intimate garden rooms reveal themselves along the way. This aerial view is atmospheric; the masterplan sets out the intended zoning.

slides.title: Stillness, framed by life.
slides.subtitle: THE CONCEPT
slides.body: A precise line of water meets loose, generous planting. Dark timber creates shelter. Pale stone catches the light. Copper tones connect seedheads, leaves and objects.
points: Strong spatial structure
Soft, layered planting
A changing experience through the year

slides.title:
Elements that age
with grace.
slides.subtitle: 02 / MATERIAL MOOD
slides.body: Pale textured limestone, buff gravel, charred timber, natural oak and weathered metal tones. A restrained family of materials allows planting and reflected light to take the lead.

slides.title:
The garden
is the artwork.
slides.subtitle: PLANTING MOOD
slides.body: Violet spires, soft mauve flowers, white glints and grasses that catch the breeze. The woodland edge becomes a quieter composition of ferns, branching trunks and deep green leaves.

slides.title: Green, in every register.
slides.subtitle: COLOUR LANGUAGE
slides.body: Forest and olive form the foundation. Chalk and copper add warmth. A muted violet note threads through the planting.

slides.title:
Designed for
more than summer.
slides.subtitle: FOUR SEASONS / ONE PLACE
slides.body: Spring blossom. Summer abundance. Autumn copper. Winter silhouette. These generated seasonal studies express the intended atmosphere; they are not records of an established garden.

slides.title:
A journey,
not just a view.
slides.subtitle: 03 / THE MASTERPLAN
slides.body: Concept zoning for an assumed 40 × 35 m garden. Arrival, water, meadow, woodland, pavilion, lounge and productive garden form one connected route. Dimensions are illustrative; this is not a measured site drawing.

slides.title:
The garden,
in three dimensions.
slides.subtitle: 3D / THE GARDEN MODEL
slides.body: A model study connects the water court, dining pavilion, circular lounge and productive beds. Simplified planting masses describe enclosure; the masterplan remains the guide to conceptual zoning.

slides.title: The quiet centre.
slides.subtitle: THE REFLECTING POOL
slides.body: A long, dark basin mirrors the sky and draws the eye through the garden. Pale coping makes a calm threshold between water and planting. A decorative water feature, conceived for reflection rather than swimming.

slides.title:
A clear frame
for still water.
slides.subtitle: 3D / WATER COURT STUDY
slides.body: Pale steps, a dark timber canopy and a reflecting basin give the garden its structure. A deliberately simple shaded model explores the relationship between these elements.

slides.title:
The first marks
of a quiet place.
slides.subtitle: CRAYON / WATER COURT SKETCH
slides.body: Loose crayon strokes explore the balance of still water, dark shelter and generous planting. Paper grain and unfinished edges preserve the feeling of an early design conversation.

slides.title:
Long lunches.
Late conversations.
slides.subtitle: THE DINING PAVILION
slides.body: Charred timber shelters a generous dining table; a slatted canopy filters the evening sun. The outdoor kitchen shown is an optional €12,800 addition to the €32,000 pavilion package.

slides.title:
Let the edges
come alive.
slides.subtitle: THE MEADOW WALK
slides.body: Drifts of airy grasses and violet perennials loosen the geometry. A gently curving path creates changing glimpses of the water and pavilion, with generous planted depth on either side.

slides.title:
Follow the
softer line.
slides.subtitle: CRAYON / MEADOW WALK SKETCH
slides.body: A winding gravel path, violet flowers and an oak bench beneath birches. A handdrawn-style study in olive, ochre and lavender, exploring movement and seasonal texture.

slides.title:
A room with
a living ceiling.
slides.subtitle: THE WOODLAND RETREAT
slides.body: Stone steps through green texture; a solid oak bench in a pocket of light. This is the quietest part of the garden, composed for a slower pace and the pleasure of small details.

slides.title: Gather a little closer.
slides.subtitle: THE SUNKEN LOUNGE
slides.body: A circular seating court offers a more intimate scale within the garden. Limestone benches and soft cushions sit just below the planted edge. Final levels, drainage and accessible circulation require coordinated technical design.

slides.title:
A garden you
can bring to the table.
slides.subtitle: THE PRODUCTIVE GARDEN
slides.body: Four oak beds, herbs, trained fruit and a working ledge make a small daily ritual. The €6,200 package includes the beds, trellis, starter planting and a simple surface water butt.

slides.title:
Plant in layers.
Read it as one.
slides.subtitle: 04 / THE PLANTING STRATEGY
slides.body: A small family of planting characters creates cohesion: meadow matrix, accent drifts, woodland carpet and structural trees. The schedule is a fictional candidate palette, subject to local soil, light and nursery review.

slides.title: Texture before colour.
slides.subtitle: THE CANDIDATE PALETTE
slides.body: Plant names describe design intent. Final cultivars, quantities and suitability are decisions for the appointed horticultural team after site assessment.

slides.title:
A landscape
with depth.
slides.subtitle: SECTION / TERRACE TO WOODLAND
slides.body: The section studies relationships between the house terrace, reflecting basin, meadow and tree canopy. Levels, depths and construction details are intentionally schematic.

slides.title:
Make room
for the rain.
slides.subtitle: WATER & SITE STRATEGY
slides.body: Coordinate drainage before the garden is built. The concept separates the decorative water feature from rainfall management, with planted collection areas and an optional storage package.
points: Confirm soil, infiltration and groundwater conditions
Resolve gradients and discharge routes with specialists
Protect existing tree root zones during works
Optional storage system: + €6,400; off by default

slides.title:
When the garden
changes its voice.
slides.subtitle: 05 / AFTER DARK
slides.body: A warm glow under the pavilion. A quiet rhythm along the path. Water holding the last colour of the sky. The dark edges remain part of the composition.

slides.title:
Light the moments.
Keep the mystery.
slides.subtitle: THE LIGHTING CONCEPT
slides.body: A scene-based lighting concept for arrival, gathering and a final evening walk. Fixture locations are indicative, not an electrical installation plan.

slides.title:
Three ways
to spend an evening.
slides.subtitle: LIGHTING SCENES
slides.body: The €12,400 lighting allowance covers fixtures, installation and commissioning. Aim, timing and ecology constraints are resolved with the appointed specialists.

slides.title:
Beautifully clear
from the ground up.
slides.subtitle: 06 / THE INVESTMENT
slides.body: €213,400–€221,400 including an €18,000 client-held contingency. Furniture selection creates the range. Optional kitchen and rainwater storage are excluded; unforeseen ground conditions remain unpriced. All figures are fictional and include assumed VAT.

slides.title:
Every layer,
accounted for.
slides.subtitle: THE SUPPLIER STRUCTURE
slides.body: Included subquotes explain a package price. Additional options increase the total only when selected. The main landscape contract is €64,000; its stone supply is visible two levels below.

slides.title:
Choose your
extra pleasures.
slides.subtitle: OPTIONS & CHOICES
slides.body: Base selection €213,400. Premium furniture adds €8,000; outdoor kitchen adds €12,800; rainwater storage adds €6,400. With all choices selected: €240,600, including contingency and excluding unpriced site conditions.

slides.title:
From first line
to first evening.
slides.subtitle: 07 / THE PROGRAMME
slides.body: An indicative 24-week delivery journey, with planting timed to the eventual site and nursery programme. The first year of establishment care follows practical handover.

slides.title:
A garden is
never quite finished.
slides.subtitle: ESTABLISHMENT & CARE
slides.body: Beauty develops through attention. The €5,200 establishment package allows for eight visits, a seasonal review and a care handover. The final regime follows the actual species and site conditions.
points: Observe establishment and respond to weather
Review irrigation and water-feature performance
Use seasonal cutbacks to retain chosen structure
Record replacements and refine the planting over time

slides.title:
Before the
first spade.
slides.subtitle: DECISIONS & SCOPE
slides.body: Approve the design direction, commission the survey, review material and planting samples, then decide on the options. Final technical design and site evidence guide the build.
points: Plans are conceptual, not construction documents
All suppliers, clients, quotations and prices are fictional
Images are generated concepts, not completed-project photos
Survey, permits, engineering and exceptional remediation excluded

slides.title: Stay a little longer.
slides.subtitle: STILLWATER GARDEN / DEMO 02
slides.body: A landscape for gathering, wandering and doing very little at all. Prepared for the fictional de Wilde family by Stillwater Landscape Studio.
